# Alternatives Comparison

Dimension comparing OPA against Casbin, Cedar, Cerbos, OSO/Polar, and OpenFGA
for Python/FastAPI API authorization. Sources: [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Summary Comparison

| Engine | Model | Language | Python SDK | FastAPI Integration | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OPA** | RBAC, ABAC, general | Rego (Datalog) | opa-python-client, fastapi-opa | Middleware package [18] | CNCF Graduated [8] |
| **Casbin** | ACL, RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC | PERM (CONF) | pycasbin | fastapi-authz [44] | Apache project [19] |
| **Cedar** | RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC | Cedar (functional) | cedar-py (unofficial) | None | AWS open source [50] |
| **Cerbos** | RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC | YAML + CEL | cerbos-sdk-python [41] | SDK available | Independent [13] |
| **OSO/Polar** | RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC | Polar | oso (PyPI) [42] | Deprecated [42] | Deprecated |
| **OpenFGA** | ReBAC (Zanzibar) | DSL | openfga-sdk [43] | SDK available | CNCF Incubating [24] |

## OPA

**Strengths**: General-purpose policy engine spanning infrastructure (Kubernetes),
CI/CD, and application authorization [13]. Mature ecosystem with CNCF graduation,
extensive tooling (Conftest, Regal, OPAL), and large community [8]. Supports
arbitrarily complex policies via Rego [1].

**Weaknesses**: Rego has a steep learning curve [13]. No built-in control plane —
requires CI/CD or Styra DAS [25]. Lower-level integration (construct JSON, parse
responses) compared to purpose-built SDKs [13].

**Performance**: 1ms evaluation target [2]. Sidecar adds 2-5ms per decision (est.) [27].

## Casbin

**Strengths**: Apache project with 16+ language implementations sharing the same
API [19]. PERM metamodel (Policy, Effect, Request, Matchers) is simpler than
Rego [19]. Official FastAPI middleware (`fastapi-authz`) [44]. Flexible policy
storage (memory, files, MySQL, Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, S3) [19]. Role manager
with external sources (LDAP, Okta, Auth0, Azure AD) [19].

**Weaknesses**: Library (not a service) — must be embedded, lacks distributed
enforcement [19]. Adopters include Intel, VMware, Docker, Cisco, Microsoft [19]
but ecosystem is less cloud-native than OPA.

**FastAPI fit**: Best if you want an embedded library with simple ACL/RBAC and
familiar CONF-style policies.

## Cedar

**Strengths**: Formal verification capabilities for policy correctness [50].
Functional language with strict typing, more readable than Rego [50].
Deny-by-default as language-level safety guarantee [50].

**Weaknesses**: AWS-centric, smaller community than OPA [50]. Python bindings
(`cedar-py`) are unofficial, not AWS-maintained. Limited tooling compared to
OPA. No standalone service deployment — library-only.

**Performance claim**: "42-60 times faster than Rego" [51]. This claim comes from
a vendor blog (Permit.io) without published benchmark methodology — treat with
skepticism.

**FastAPI fit**: Poor — no official Python SDK, no FastAPI integration, no service
mode.

## Cerbos

**Strengths**: Purpose-built for application/API authorization [13]. Declarative
YAML + Google CEL — minimal training needed [13]. Stateless architecture supports
service, sidecar, serverless, embedded [13]. Official Python SDK with async
support [41]. High-level SDK with `isAllowed()` calls, built-in testing, audit
logging, visual Playground [13].

**Weaknesses**: Not general-purpose — focused on application authorization only [13].
Smaller community than OPA [13].

**Performance**: Claims "up to 17× faster" than their prior OPA-based engine,
"fraction of a millisecond of CPU time" [13]. This is a vendor claim —
independent verification not available.

**FastAPI fit**: Strong — async Python SDK, purpose-built for API authorization,
simpler policy language.

## OSO / Polar

**Strengths**: Purpose-built authorization library for application code. Polar
language designed for authorization specifically.

**Weaknesses**: **Project is deprecated** [42]. Still receives critical bug fixes
but no new development. Not a viable choice for new projects.

## OpenFGA

**Strengths**: CNCF Incubating project implementing Google Zanzibar ReBAC model [24].
Official Python SDK with async support [43]. Millisecond-level response times [24].
Adopters include Auth0, Docker, Grafana, Okta, Sourcegraph [24].

**Weaknesses**: Optimized for ReBAC (relationship-based) — not ideal for pure
RBAC or ABAC without a relationship model. Requires relationship tuple storage
infrastructure. No FastAPI-specific integration.

**FastAPI fit**: Good if your authorization model is primarily relationship-based
(e.g., "user X is editor of document Y").

## Decision Framework

**Choose OPA if**: You need policy enforcement across infrastructure AND
application layers, have Go expertise or can tolerate Rego's learning curve,
want CNCF-graduated maturity, or need Kubernetes admission control alongside
API authorization.

**Choose Casbin if**: You want an embedded library with simple policy syntax, need
the official FastAPI middleware, prefer CONF-file configuration over a DSL, and
don't need distributed policy enforcement.

**Choose Cerbos if**: Your primary need is application/API authorization, you want
the simplest developer experience (YAML policies, isAllowed() SDK), and you value
purpose-built tooling over general-purpose flexibility.

**Choose OpenFGA if**: Your authorization model is relationship-heavy (documents,
organizations, teams), you want Zanzibar-style graph-based access control, and
you're comfortable with the CNCF incubating maturity level.

**Avoid Cedar for Python/FastAPI**: No official Python SDK, no FastAPI integration,
library-only deployment.

**Avoid OSO/Polar**: Deprecated project.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Cedar's "42-60× faster" claim [51] lacks published benchmark methodology —
  cannot be independently verified
- Cerbos's "17× faster" claim [13] is self-reported after migrating their own
  engine — not an OPA-to-OPA comparison
- No independent benchmark comparing all engines under identical conditions
  with Python/FastAPI
- Trail of Bits assessment [26] was referenced but full report not publicly
  accessible during this research
- Long-term OPA maintenance concern: Apple hired OPA maintainers in August 2025
  (unverified claim from discovery agent — could not confirm via fetched sources)
